_note: v13.1: v13 with one change, loss_weights.ssl 5 -> 20. In v13 the SSL loss rose from 0.069 to ~0.080 while the supervised losses fell, so at weight 5 the term never held the local and global views together and the idea was not really tested (v13 val HM 56.53 vs v5.5 56.89). Weight 20 should make the SSL loss actually fall. Compare with v5.5 (56.89; keep only if > 58.9) and v13. Everything else as v13 (see its _note).
_result: Validation HM 55.65% (epoch 10, gamma 0.0625) vs v5.5 56.89% (-1.2 pts) and v13 56.53%: below the +2 bar, NOT kept. The SSL loss now held (0.042-0.049 throughout, vs v13's 0.069 rising to 0.080), so the idea was tested properly this time and still did not raise validation HM. Test (diagnostic only, not used for the decision): HM 68.31 / Top-5 92.08, seen 58.45, unseen 82.18 (v5.5: 64.48, 52.20, 84.32). Uncalibrated: seen crop 91.10 / disease 70.60 (v5.5 90.85 / 69.40), similar gains, so no lesion-specific effect; raw unseen Top-1 fell to 18.30 (v5.5 28.73).
title: ssl_weight20

model._note: Same OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16 (QuickGELU) as v4.1/v4.2; the text encoder stays frozen.

image_encoder._note: From v5.3: v5 + more LoRA capacity: last 8 blocks instead of 4, rank 16 instead of 8. alpha 16 -> 32 keeps the LoRA scale (alpha/rank) at 2, so only capacity changes, not the effective step size. About 4x more adapter parameters (1.57M vs 393k). Same lr.

input._note: Images come from the 256 px resize cache (runs/cache/resized_256, shared with the CNN baselines). Test: CLIP's resize 224 + centre crop + CLIP mean/std. The app must standardise uploads the same way (dpd/resize_cache.standardise).

augmentation._note: Same as the CNN baselines except a milder crop scale (0.5-1 instead of 0.25-1), because CLIP's pretrained features expect whole-object views. No hue jitter: colour is diagnostic.

ssl_local._note: NEW: local view for the SSL loss. Scale floor 0.1 so most crops still contain leaf tissue. Flips as the global view. batch_fraction 1 = every image gets a local view (lower it only if GPU memory runs out).

validation._note: Same procedure as v4.2 but 1 split instead of 3: each split is now a full training run with the image encoder in the loop (images instead of cached embeddings). Note v4.2 showed one split can mis-set gamma, so treat v5's gamma with that caveat.

training._note: Prompt vectors as v4.2 (AdamW lr 2e-4, weight decay 0, logit scale 100, loss weights pair 1 / crop 0.5 / disease 0.5). max_epochs 30 -> 15 (v4.1/v4.2 selected epochs 13-18 with cached features; each epoch now re-encodes every image). Batch 256 -> 64 for GPU memory with gradients through 4 image-encoder blocks. CHANGED (v13): loss_weights.ssl 5 (local-to-global self-supervised loss, see augmentation.ssl_local). Weight 5, not 0.5: the supervised losses use logit scale 100, so per unit of cosine their gradients are about 100x larger than the SSL term's; the smoke test's SSL loss started at ~0.10 (local and global CLS already ~0.9 cosine), so 0.5 would be negligible. 5 puts the SSL gradient at roughly 10% of the cross-entropy's; weights 2 and 10 are the planned ablations. CHANGED (v13.1): loss_weights.ssl 20.

runtime._note: Gradient checkpointing on the text encoder as before. 4 dataloader workers read the resize cache. CHANGED (v13): grad_checkpointing_image true. Compute only (same results up to GPU nondeterminism): the local view doubles the images per step, and without it the smoke test peaked at 8.1 GiB on the 6 GiB GPU (spilled to shared memory, ~10x slower).
